??? MEENGLE - SAFETY TIPS FOR SOUTH AFRICA

Your safety is our top priority. Follow these guidelines to have a safe and positive experience on MEENGLE in South Africa.

?? Protecting Your Account

Use a Strong, Unique Password

Create a password with at least 12 characters including uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols. Don't use the same password on other websites.

Enable Two-Factor Authentication

Go to Settings ? Security ? Two-Factor Authentication. This adds an extra layer of protection to your account.

Never Share Your Password

MEENGLE will never ask for your password via email or message. If someone does, it's a scam. Report it immediately.

Keep Your Email Secure

Your email is tied to your MEENGLE account. Use a secure email with a strong password and two-factor authentication.

?? Profile & Photo Safety

Use Recent, Clear Photos

Post recent photos that clearly show your face. This helps people recognize you and builds trust.

Don't Share Identifying Information in Bio

Avoid including your full name, workplace, home address, phone number, or social media in your profile until you trust someone.

Never Post Explicit Photos

Don't share nude, semi-nude, or sexually explicit images. They can be screenshot, shared, or used for blackmail. This is illegal in South Africa under certain circumstances.

Be Cautious with Location Sharing

Don't share your exact location, workplace, gym, or places you frequent until you've met someone in person.

?? Safe Messaging Practices

Take Time Before Meeting

Message for at least a week before agreeing to meet. Get to know their personality, interests, and values.

Verify Their Story

Ask questions about their life, job, interests, and background. Look for consistency. Inconsistencies may indicate catfishing.

Trust Your Instincts

If something feels off about someone�weird questions, lack of detail, rushing to meet�trust your gut. It's okay to unmatch.

Never Send Money

This is a huge red flag. Legitimate people you're dating won't ask for money. Ever. Not for flights, emergencies, or investments.

?? Be Wary of These Red Flags:
  • They ask for money or Bitcoin
  • They claim to love you after knowing you a few days
  • Their photos look like they belong to a model
  • They only have 1-2 photos
  • They refuse to video call before meeting
  • They claim to be "newly in town" and don't know people
  • They ask you to move conversations to WhatsApp/text immediately
  • They claim to be rich/traveling/mysterious

?? Meeting in Person Safety (South African Context)

???? SOUTH AFRICA SAFETY:

South Africa has higher crime rates than some countries. Taking extra precautions when meeting online dates is important:

Always Meet in Safe, Public Places

Choose busy public places with good security:

  • Johannesburg: Sandton, Menlyn, The Grove, Rosebank
  • Cape Town: V&A Waterfront, Camps Bay, Constantia
  • Durban: The Pavilion, Umhlanga Ridges, Beachfront
  • Pretoria: The Woodsman, Hatfield, Menlyn
  • Other areas: Coffee shops, restaurants, shopping malls with security

Never agree to meet at their home, your home, or isolated locations on a first date.

  • Tell a trusted friend or family member exactly where you're going and who you're meeting
  • Share your location with a friend via WhatsApp or Google Maps during the date
  • Set up a time to text your friend when you arrive safely
  • Arrange your own transportation (use Uber, Bolt, or Indriver rather than carpooling)
  • Keep your phone charged and accessible at all times
  • Have a safety call setup (friend calls you after 30 mins to check in)
  • Know how you're getting home in advance�have your ride arranged
  • Meet during daylight hours for first meetings when possible
Do a Video Call First

Before meeting, do a video call to verify they're who they claim to be. Legitimate people will be happy to video chat.

Take Time on First Dates

Plan for a short first date (30-60 minutes at a coffee shop or restaurant). It's easier to extend if it's going well than to cut it short if it's not.

?? If You Feel Unsafe:
  • Excuse yourself to the bathroom and call a friend or security
  • Leave immediately if you feel threatened
  • Don't worry about being rude�safety comes first
  • Tell nearby staff members or security if you're in danger
  • Call South African Police (SAPS) on 10177 or emergency services on 112
  • Go to the nearest police station if needed

?? Reporting & Blocking

Report Suspicious Behavior

If someone harasses, threatens, or scams you, report them immediately. Click the ? menu and select "Report." Our team reviews all reports within 24 hours. Serious crimes will be reported to SAPS.

Block Users Who Make You Uncomfortable

You don't need a reason to block someone. If they weird you out, block them. They won't be able to message or see your profile.

Don't Engage with Scammers

If you suspect a scam, stop engaging. Don't argue with them. Block and report them. They're trying to manipulate you.

?? Financial Safety

?? NEVER:
  • Send money to someone you haven't met in person
  • Share credit card information via message
  • Participate in "make money fast" schemes promoted by matches
  • Invest in cryptocurrencies suggested by matches
  • Buy gift cards at their request
  • Pay for "verification fees" or anything similar
Be Cautious with Payment Information

MEENGLE's payment system is secure with Stripe and South African payment providers. Only enter payment info on our official app/website, never via message or external links.

?? General Safety Reminders

  • Be yourself�authenticity is attractive and safe
  • Take your time getting to know someone
  • Trust your gut feeling about people
  • Keep personal information private until you trust someone
  • Don't feel obligated to respond to anyone
  • It's okay to end conversations anytime
  • Report anything that violates our community guidelines
  • Remember that MEENGLE team members will never ask for passwords or personal info via message
  • Have fun, but stay alert
  • Dating should be enjoyable, not stressful

?? SOUTH AFRICAN EMERGENCY & SUPPORT CONTACTS

If You Experience Crime or Harassment:
  • SAPS (South African Police Service): 10177 (toll-free) or 0860 10 10 10
  • Emergency Services: 112 (from mobile)
  • SAPS Crime Line: 086 001 0600
  • Rape Crisis (Sexual Assault): 0800 35 2500 (24/7)
  • Gender-Based Violence Hotline: 0800 050 150
  • Sexual Offences Unit: Ask SAPS for nearest station

?? If You Encounter These Scams

Romance Scam: Person claims to fall in love quickly, makes excuses not to meet in person, eventually asks for money for "emergency" or "travel." (REPORT & BLOCK)
Catfishing: Using fake photos or false information. Refuses video call before meeting. (REPORT & BLOCK)
Investment Scam: Matches promote crypto, forex trading, or "business opportunities" to make quick money. (REPORT & BLOCK)
Photo Extortion: Someone asks for explicit photos, then threatens to share them unless you pay. (REPORT & CONTACT SAPS)
Robbery Setup: Someone arranges to meet then doesn't show up / tries to lure you to unsafe location. (TRUST YOUR INSTINCTS & LEAVE)

Emergency:

Your safety is our responsibility. Stay smart, stay safe, and have fun on MEENGLE! ??
